guideTitle: 6 Best Dustpan and Brush Sets Under $20 in 2026
metaTitle: Best Dustpan and Brush Sets Under $20 in 2026
metaDescription: Six handheld dustpan and brush sets under a mid-small budget, compared on pan lip, hair-cleaning combs, bristle type and how each set stores.
introParagraphs: Moving up a tier changes the question from which set is smallest to which set handles the awkward messes: hair, lint and fine dust that sit on a hard floor. The sets here all remain handheld, so the bending limitation stays, but the feature differences get more interesting. Two of the six now carry comb teeth to strip hair from the bristles, and the pan lips range from silicone strips to a wide flexible edge.

We evaluated six distinct listings: the WDDBHSKN set with scraper teeth, the OXO Good Grips set, the Amazon Basics two-pack, the nacena mini set, the Pine-Sol mini set and the Casabella Wayclean. Judgments rest on listed bristle materials, pan lip construction, comb features and storage design. The Amazon Basics two-pack counts as one listing even though it contains two sets.

The pattern at this cap is that you can finally choose a set built around how hair and fine grit behave, instead of simply buying the smallest option. If your messes are mostly crumbs, you can still save with a mini. If hair is the daily problem, aim for a comb.

products.badge: Best for Pet and Human Hair
products.name: WDDBHSKN Dustpan and Brush Set with Comb Teeth
products.description:
The WDDBHSKN set is built around hair removal. The dustpan carries a built-in scraper and comb teeth, and the listing says pet hair and human hair come off in one pull. The bristles are PET fibers, and the handles are ergonomically designed with a non-slip grip.

The wide lip is described as giving maximum surface area for sweeping debris in. Together with the comb, it addresses the two most frustrating parts of a handheld set: hair that tangles in the bristles and debris that slips past a narrow edge. The listing does not state the lip material or dimensions, so confirm on the product page whether the lip is soft.

In daily use the routine is sweep, drag the bristles across the teeth, then empty. Compared with the Casabella Wayclean, which also has a built-in comb, the WDDBHSKN emphasizes the wide lip and a scraper. Against the OXO Good Grips, which has no comb, it is the better choice where hair is constant.
products.bestFor: Homes with pets or long hair where the brush needs frequent cleaning.
pros: Comb teeth strip hair from the bristles
Wide lip for maximum surface area

products.name: OXO Good Grips Dustpan and Brush Set
products.description:
The OXO Good Grips set uses a whisk-broom brush with nylon bristles to sweep from above and reach into corners. Its dustpan has a soft flexible lip that covers the whole pan width and conforms to surfaces. The brush snaps into the pan, so the pair stores together.

The conforming lip is the reason to pick it: it follows slight unevenness in a floor or counter and closes the gap that stiff lips leave. The listing does not describe a comb, so hair has to be pulled from the bristles by hand. Size details are not given, so check the product page.

It is a calm, dependable set rather than a feature pile. Compared with the WDDBHSKN, the OXO has no comb but has the snap-in storage that keeps parts together. Next to the nacena, the OXO relies on a full-width flexible lip rather than silicone strips.
products.bestFor: A single reliable set with a flexible full-width lip.
pros: Flexible lip spans the full pan width

products.name: Casabella Wayclean Handheld Angled Dustpan and Brush
products.description:
Casabella's Wayclean is a medium handheld set with a pointed tip brush for corners and cracks, with rubber bumpers that protect walls. The dustpan has a built-in comb for cleaning dust off the brush, and a soft rubber lip lies flat against the floor.

The pointed tip is its own selling point. Most handheld brushes are blunt or whisk-shaped, and a pointed tip gets into the line where floor meets baseboard. The comb is useful but the listing describes it as cleaning dust rather than specifically hair. It is medium sized, so it holds more per trip than a mini.

In practice it suits a hallway or stair run. Compared with the WDDBHSKN, the Casabella leans on corner reach and wall protection while the WDDBHSKN leans on a wide lip and scraper. Next to the Pine-Sol mini, it is larger and stores less compactly.
products.bestFor: Baseboards, stair corners and cracks where a blunt brush cannot reach.
cons: Comb described for dust, not hair

products.name: nacena Mini Broom and Dustpan Set
products.description:
The nacena mini set pairs ultra-fine high-density fiber bristles with silicone strips along the dustpan edge. The listing says the strips fit tightly against a tabletop and prevent spillage when dumping. The handle is electroplated ABS, and the pan is described as anti-slip and wear-resistant.

It is the best fit for flat surfaces, because silicone closes the gap where fine dust slips under a rigid lip. The mini size limits capacity, and the listing gives no bristle length. There is no comb on the pan.

Compared with the Amazon Basics pack, which gives two mini sets with a flush rubber lip, the nacena is a single set with silicone strips. Against the WDDBHSKN, it has no comb and a smaller pan, so it is better for tables than for hair-heavy floors.
products.bestFor: Tabletops and counters where fine dust slips past a hard edge.
pros: Silicone strips seal on flat surfaces
Ultra-fine bristles pick up small debris

products.name: Amazon Basics Mini Dustpan and Brush Set 2-Pack
products.description:
Amazon Basics provides two mini sets built from resilient polypropylene and PET plastic. The dustpan edge has a flush rubber lip, and the brush is angled with flexible bristles to collect fine dust from corners. The listing positions the pack for indoor and outdoor use.

The pack of two is the draw. One set can stay in the kitchen while the other goes to a car, shed or bedside. The rubber lip seals better than a hard edge. Neither set has a comb, and the listing gives no nesting storage.

Compared with the OXO Good Grips, you get two small sets instead of one larger one. Next to the Pine-Sol, which nests as a single piece, the Amazon Basics gives a spare in exchange for less compact storage.
products.bestFor: Keeping one set in two places, such as kitchen and car.

products.name: Pine-Sol Mini Dustpan and Brush Set
products.description:
Pine-Sol offers a mini set with a nesting snap-on design so the pair stores as one piece. The brush has a whisk shape, and the listing mentions tables, desks, camping, RVs and dorms. It is the most portable set here.

Its compact size is the whole point. It holds little and has no stated comb or lip material, so it is best for dry crumbs and dust. For anything bigger the pan is soon full.

Compared with the WDDBHSKN, the Pine-Sol is a travel-size sweeper without hair features. Next to the nacena mini, it puts nesting ahead of a sealed edge.
products.bestFor: Desks, dorms and RVs where space matters more than capacity.

buyingCriteria.explanation: A comb or teeth on the pan rim cleans hair from bristles. The WDDBHSKN lists scraper and comb teeth that clear pet and human hair in one pull, and the Casabella lists a built-in comb. The OXO, nacena, Amazon Basics and Pine-Sol list none. If a pet sheds or a long-haired family lives in the home, this is the first feature to filter by. Hair left in bristles also makes a brush smear dust on the next pass, so a comb improves sweeping as well as tidiness. The Pine-Sol at mini size has no such feature, which is fine if the mess is crumbs.

A soft flexible lip spanning the pan width seals gaps, while a rigid lip leaves one. The OXO lists a full-width soft lip, the Amazon Basics a flush rubber lip, and the Casabella a soft rubber lip that lies flat. The WDDBHSKN lists a wide lip but not its material. Check the product page when fine dust is the main concern. A wide lip such as the WDDBHSKN lists reduces how many passes you need, though a stiff wide lip still leaves a gap.

PET synthetic bristles are durable and easy to clean, and the WDDBHSKN and Amazon Basics list PET. The OXO uses nylon and the nacena uses ultra-fine fiber. Medium-stiff compact bristles reach corners without splaying. Pick the material that matches the surface and mess. The Casabella and OXO do not state bristle length, so shape and material are the differences you can actually compare.

A pointed tip gets into cracks along the baseboard, and rubber bumpers protect walls from scuffs. The Casabella is the only one that lists both. An angled brush such as the Amazon Basics also reaches into corners. If stairs and baseboards are your main use, put reach first. The nacena and Pine-Sol minis do not list a corner feature, so they suit open surfaces more than tight gaps.

A brush that snaps into the pan stores compactly and covers the bristles. The OXO snaps in and the Pine-Sol nests. The two-pack from Amazon Basics gives you a spare, which is a different kind of convenience. Check the product page for hanging holes, since wall storage keeps the set in reach. The WDDBHSKN and nacena list no storage feature, so plan a hook or drawer spot for them.

Upright long-handled dustpans avoid kneeling, while handheld sets require bending. All six picks here are handheld and designed for counters, tables, stairs and spills. If you cannot bend to the floor comfortably, these are the wrong category. For everything else, a handheld set is the right size. For a person who struggles with floor-level work, a handheld set still helps on a counter or stair tread within reach.

howWeEvaluated.title: Hair handling
howWeEvaluated.description: We looked for combs or teeth on the pan. The WDDBHSKN lists scraper and comb teeth, and the Casabella lists a built-in comb. The other four have none. Hair removal carries the most weight at this cap. The WDDBHSKN pairs the comb with PET bristles, while the Casabella pairs it with a pointed tip.

howWeEvaluated.title: Pan lip construction
howWeEvaluated.description: We read how each lip is described: full-width soft lip for the OXO, flush rubber for the Amazon Basics, silicone strips for the nacena and soft rubber for the Casabella. The WDDBHSKN lists a wide lip with no material. Sealing edges scored higher than undescribed ones. The OXO and Casabella are the two that describe a soft lip that conforms or lies flat.

howWeEvaluated.title: Brush design
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared pointed, angled, whisk and ultra-fine designs. The Casabella leads for corners, the nacena for fine dust and the WDDBHSKN for hair when paired with the comb. The Pine-Sol and OXO use whisk shapes. Bristle length is mostly unlisted, so shape decided. We avoided inferring performance from the word fine or ultra-fine alone.

howWeEvaluated.title: Storage and portability
howWeEvaluated.description: We noted snap-in storage on the OXO and nesting on the Pine-Sol. The Amazon Basics scores for two sets. The WDDBHSKN and nacena list no storage feature. Portability favors the mini sets. The WDDBHSKN lists no storage method at all, which counts against it for small kitchens.

howWeEvaluated.title: Value at this cap
howWeEvaluated.description: Every pick is within the cap, so value means what the set adds. The WDDBHSKN adds hair cleaning, the Casabella adds corner reach, and the OXO adds a full-width lip. The Amazon Basics adds a second set. We did not use pricing in the text.

faq.q: Which set handles pet hair best?
faq.a: Look for comb or scraper teeth on the pan. The WDDBHSKN lists scraper and comb teeth that clear pet and human hair in one pull, and the Casabella lists a comb as well. The other four have none, so hair must be removed by hand. For constant shedding, the WDDBHSKN is the focused choice. If you only occasionally sweep pet hair, the Casabella gives a comb and a more compact medium size.

faq.q: Is the OXO a better choice than the cheaper minis?
faq.a: It depends on the lip and the size. The OXO lists a soft flexible lip across the full pan width and a snap-in brush. The minis such as the Pine-Sol are smaller and nest, but give no lip detail. If you want fewer gaps for fine dust, the OXO is the better design. If you pay for the OXO, you are paying for lip quality and storage rather than a comb.

faq.q: Do I need a medium set or is a mini enough?
faq.a: A mini suits crumbs, dust and desk spills. A medium such as the Casabella holds more per trip. Think of how often you want to walk to the trash. For larger messes, a medium or upright option saves trips. The Pine-Sol and nacena are the smallest sets here.

A soft flexible lip seals the gap where fine dust escapes, while a rigid plastic lip leaves a gap. The OXO, Amazon Basics, nacena and Casabella all describe soft, rubber or silicone edges. The WDDBHSKN lists a wide lip but not its material. Fine dust on hard floors shows the difference.

faq.q: Are two small sets better than one big one?
faq.a: Two sets help when you sweep in different rooms. The Amazon Basics pack gives two minis with a flush rubber lip. One medium set such as the Casabella is better for bigger messes. Pick by how many places need a set. The nacena and Pine-Sol are single minis, so they suit one location.

faq.q: How do I keep bristles in good shape?
faq.a: Clean hair off regularly, using the comb where the set has one. Store the brush so the bristles are not bent, such as snapped into the pan on the OXO or nested on the Pine-Sol. PET and nylon bristles keep their shape when not crushed. Avoid leaving the brush on its bristles.
